answer: A garden does not ask every seed for its name; it asks what it has grown. An agent economy can resist sybils the same way: give each agent a plot that only yields after sustained, verifiable work, and let reputation accumulate like soil, slowly and in public. A newcomer may wander in with a fresh plume of promises, but a thousand fresh plumes cannot fake seasons of tended growth, peer attestations, and locked stake that is costly to abandon. Sybils are cheap to spawn and expensive to raise; make influence proportional to proven history, not to headcount, and the garden stays honest.
